This went on through our Stepmother's dementia and her death and then getting my father's house ready to sell, selling that and then moving him to an attached apartment we made by remodeling our attached garage. Then I was the sole caretaker of my dad, who was by then 91 years old. Then it was all the driving to the doctors, driving to the hospital after all the falls, broken hip and surgery, broken foot and the big black boot, and concussion and stitches and Rehab, so many other things like that. For 5 years and then this May he died. I thought I would feel relieved that he was gone because it was so stressful every day and all night. But you know what, I miss him so much. And I wish he was still here. I loved my old dad.😢

I was pretty much solely responsible for advocating for my dad after he suffered a major heart attack while having my mom Dx with mid-stage alzheimers in the midst of it, because my dad refused to take her to see a neurologist. He ended up passing away a month later, and my mother, unfortunately, was out of it, so I had to handle all the arrangements for his funeral/burial.
She refused to move in with me, and because we lived in another state, I was forced to commute every other month to make sure she was doing well. Thankfully she had some friends and family who checked in on her constantly and kept me informed of any events. It really impacted us financially speaking, not mention the stress of it all. It took 2 years and a nasty fall to finally get her moved in with me and my spouse. Then it was a broken hip that forced us to make the unavoidable decision to move her to a senior living facility a few years later. I can say I aged a decade in the few years I was in charge of her care and I don't believe I've ever recovered from the stress of it. My brain and health have never been the same.

snippet.textDisplay:
Girl, I am WITH you.

In the last 10 years I gained 80 lbs. EIGHTY POUNDS. Hormones were off since the birth of my last child in my early 30s (I’m now 49, almost 50) and was getting prometrium and T3 supplementation until it wasn’t working anymore. Fast forward ~5 years and Covid hit at the same time I inherited the care and responsibility of my dying father. Dad was so ill and helpless that it was like parenting him. I managed his care for over a year until he died alone in a hospital during Covid (I’ll never get over not being there with him) while my ailing mother went to live in another state with my brother so he could manage her care as she waited for the hospitals to open back up for her heart surgery. Dad died. I gained more weight, felt depressed, no motivation, couldn’t sleep. Missed a lot of work to be with sick mother who we believed was near death several times over the last 3 years. I also missed a lot of time with my husband and kids during their middle and high school years due to my parent’s high needs and inability to care for themselves or each other. I don’t regret the sacrifices but it was very, very tough.

Fast forward to this year as mom continued to get sicker and is too much for my brother even when she’s in a nursing home facility. She cries when she’s alone and we’re not with her. Mom is very high needs and dependent on us like a small child with advanced dementia and worsening anxiety and depression and uncontrollable emotions. It’s like we’re parenting her and have been for years. Mom has been on hospice for over a year, then was removed from it just before her last two hospitalizations this month.

In the last three weeks she’s been in the hospital twice and has declined severely, with worsening dementia and critical health issues that she’s too frail to be treated for. I lost my job in June, have a problematic adult child causing us major stress, and have been driving to another state weekly to be with my mother in the hospital or in her nursing home, in what feels like parenting a terminally ill, needy child.

We thought my mom was dying the afternoon I drove back home last week to prep for my final job interview, and I felt so guilty for feeling anger and frustration at her for this timing (that she could not help!)…because I had to decide between turning around to go back to her to be with her while she passed away or miss the critical interview and jeopardize the job. This was a no-win situation. It was an awful, guilty feeling, and all through this I developed horrible sciatica that has had me in agony these past 4 weeks, but I haven’t been able to tend to it with a doctor because I’ve been with my sick mother most of this time.

I just discovered your videos and got your book a month ago, and somehow fit in some video appts with my primary care and ObGyn docs to get bloodwork and start HRT. I’ve been feeling awful for years and didn’t realize how badly I have been missing out on life. All of this has caused great strain on my marriage. So yeah, it’s been an awful summer and awful past several years. Piled on top of this I discovered I’m probably in late perimenopause.

Hopefully I can find relief from this brain fog and insomnia before starting my new job in a few weeks. I need to feel better for myself and my family. These last several years have been the most difficult in my life.

My female ob-gyn and primary care doctors don’t seem to know much about perimenopause or menopause and I had to fight, armed with resources from you, to just get a scrip for the combi-patch this past week. Thank you for your videos, Dr. Haver!

snippet.textDisplay: I’m 46 & the oldest grandchild. My mother passed in 2012 so the care for my grandmother (who raised me) & her 2 sisters, plus my dad has fallen in me. My siblings & cousins are either estranged due to issues that go back decades or they’ve moved off & just live their own lives & don’t think twice about us here. It’s very difficult to watch them age & lose independence & live in constant pain/ discomfort. They range in age from 65-90. I’m grateful none had dementia so they have agency. I just wish I wasnt always in a hurry with them. Always going here & there & treated this & that. I’m always in a dread run putting out fires & taking care of business. The opportunity to sit & chat or enjoy a meal never seems to come anymore. Most conversations revolve around ailments, aches, pains, medications, procedures & preparations for death. It’s definitely not what I thought this period of my life would be like.

snippet.textDisplay:
I'm so sorry for everyone who has to watch and/or care for and worry endlessly for their aging parents. It is heartbreaking 💔
I'm 54...lost my dad at age 75, 15 yrs ago (he was an alcoholic, which contributed to his demise 😢). Lost my mum eight years later, after moving her closer to me and watching her go downhill over a 2/3 year span. She had osteoporosis, and chronic back pain and arthritis. She was smart as a whip, until she wasn't 😩. This was while my kids were young and it was like having a fourth child, but a thousand times worse. She had dementia symptoms very often that I now know was likely due to UTI's. She fell ALOT, and needed a walker. I finally had to place her in a long-term care facility (kicking and screaming). In the 2nd week there she fell and broke her pelvis. She barely walked after that...and passed away less than 2 mths later. I had no idea at the time that lack of hormones was THE reason her health declined at such a steady rate from about 50 onward...she suffered in pain for over 30 YEARS😭.

I cared for my mother-in-law as well. She was diagnosed at 65 with Alzheimer's disease and we watched her decline for ten years before she passed...so sad.

I am changing this outcome in our family!!!! I quit alcohol, I'm in therapy, I am OBSESSED with all the info about peri/post menopause. I can look back now and see that the majority of my health problems started a few years after my 3rd daughter was born at age 38, sooo maybe 42ish.
I asked my doctor to put me on MHT last year (I'm in Ontario, Canada) and I'm on the highest estrogen transdermal, vaginal estrogen, and oral progesterone. I've asked for Testosterone as well, but she will not test my hormone levels, nor prescribe me it. She referred me to an Endocrinologist (male), who dismissed me and said I'd grow hair all over my body🤬, and wouldn't listen to any of my concerns. I am now on an 18 month waiting list to see an OBGYN. Ridiculous!
I just got my doctor to prescribe DHEA (vaginal suppository daily), as that's the closest I could get to Testosterone🙄
I am now, a WOMAN on a MISSION!!!!! I WILL somehow get my levels checked and get on TRT Testosterone AND then I'm going to shout it to the world, and make sure more women know ALL the information (starting with my own three daughters!)
First stop will be the National Menopause Show in Toronto in October!!! Thank you Dr Haver for sharing your knowledge with us!! I am forever grateful and will pass on what I've learned/am still learning to every woman I can!!🩷

Yes I am. My mother just turned 89 and my dad will be 87 in November.
Neither are in the best of health. My dad has heart issues and I think dementia is approaching. My mother has severe scoliosis and sciatica. We had a heated discussion earlier this month about looking at sheltered accommodation. They didn't want to do that. However they wanted me to move back to the UK (I live in Spain where my late hubby and I built our forever home) and we pool our resources so I can have a granny annexe! I have 5 cats, 2 of them won't survive the journey plus putting them in an environment with 2 people approaching 90?! I don't think so!
Also it's too expensive for me to move back plus the strain on me, so close to losing my darling hubby😢
It's extremely difficult but what really frustrates me is I'm trying to help them to help themselves. Dad still drives and they want to go cruising. In a sheltered apartment, they'll have little jobs to do not a great long list!
It took my husband and I YEARS to get them to agree to get a gardener and cleaner!
I love them dearly and I help when I visit but moving back to the UK will kill me. I'm asthmatic. All my years in the UK, every winter I got chest infections so severe, they landed me in hospital. In Spain, nada.
I feel selfish and torn but also resolute and determined.
If they won't help themselves, how can I help them?
